correctness.rationale: Every reversal-invariant binary length-eight code is a union of reversal orbits. Exhaustive evaluation retains exactly 56 internally admissible orbits (12 singleton, 44 doubleton), with 929 pairwise-compatibility edges. A valid code is a weighted clique; exhaustive maximal-clique search (2107 cliques, graph optimum weight 18) proves the upper bound. Full seven-shift, all-ordered-triples testing—not merely the necessary pairwise graph test—filters sixteen graph-optimal cliques to exactly twelve true eighteen-word codes. Since a same-weight clique cannot be properly contained under the proven weight bound, these exhaust all optimal codes. Explicit complete witnesses, two independently programmed exact graph and overlap enumerators, and a separate check of six-palindrome/six-reversal-pair and complement structure corroborate the proof. The claim is only for a finite domain; no infinite or external certification is asserted.

value.rationale: The directly motivating Churchill study introduces reversal-closed comma-free dictionaries and seeks tight answers at even lengths. Exact size and all equality cases at binary blocklength eight are a natural finite extremal invariant, not an arbitrary slice: the classification identifies real combinatorial constraints beyond pairwise compatibility, the full symmetry structure of optimizers, and explicit complete optimal dictionaries. Unrestricted comma-free and strong/nonoverlapping maxima do not answer it. No unproved universal extension, practical gain, or unsupported priority claim is needed for its finite mathematical value.
